subject: physics
topic: Scalars and vectors, resolution of forces

kept.q: A crate on a rough horizontal floor is pulled by a force F = 40 N applied at an angle theta above the horizontal. If the component of F along the horizontal direction that moves the crate is 20 N, what is the value of theta?
kept.explanation: The horizontal component is F cos(theta), so cos(theta) = 20/40 = 0.5, which gives theta = 60°.
kept.pidgin: To find theta, you go use di formula F cos(theta). When you divide 20 by 40, you go get 0.5. Dat one mean say theta na 60°.

kept.q: Two forces act on a particle: P = 12 N directed along the positive x-axis, and Q = 9 N directed along the positive y-axis. What is the magnitude of the single force that would exactly balance (cancel out) the resultant of P and Q?
kept.explanation: The resultant of the two perpendicular forces is sqrt(12^2 + 9^2) = 15 N. The equilibrant must have the same magnitude as this resultant but act in the opposite direction, so its magnitude is 15 N.
kept.pidgin: Di resultant of di two forces wey dey perpendicular na sqrt(12^2 + 9^2) wey be 15 N. Di equilibrant suppose get di same magnitude, so e still be 15 N.

kept.q: Three forces act on a ring that is in equilibrium on a smooth table: a force of 8 N pulling due east, a force of 8 N pulling due west, and a third force. What must be true of the third force for equilibrium to be maintained?
options: It must be 16 N directed due north
It must be zero, since the two 8 N forces already cancel
It must be 8 N directed due north
It must be 11.3 N directed due north
kept.explanation: The 8 N east and 8 N west forces are equal and opposite, so they already sum to zero; for the ring to remain in equilibrium the third force must itself be zero (no extra force needed).
kept.pidgin: Di 8 N wey dey east and di 8 N wey dey west don cancel each other finish. So, no extra force dey needed again, wey mean say di third force must be zero.

kept.q: A wooden block of mass 5 kg rests on a rough inclined plane that makes an angle of 37° with the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s^2 and sin 37° = 0.6, what is the component of the block's weight acting along the incline (down the slope)?
kept.explanation: The weight of the block is mg = 5 x 10 = 50 N. The component along the incline is mg sin(theta) = 50 x 0.6 = 30 N.
kept.pidgin: Di weight of di block na mg = 5 x 10 = 50 N. To get di component along di incline, you multiply 50 by sin 37° and dat go give you 30 N.

kept.q: Four coplanar forces act at a point: 10 N due east, 10 N due north, 10 N due west, and 10 N due south. What is the magnitude of the resultant force on the point?
kept.explanation: The east and west forces cancel (10 N - 10 N = 0), and the north and south forces also cancel (10 N - 10 N = 0), leaving a net resultant of zero newtons.
kept.pidgin: Di force wey dey east go cancel di one wey dey west, and di north one go cancel south. Everything cancelout finish, so di net resultant force na zero newtons.

q.q: A pilot wishes to fly an aircraft due north. The aircraft's engine can give it a speed of 200 km/h in still air, but a wind of 60 km/h is blowing from the west (that is, towards the east). What is the resultant speed of the aircraft relative to the ground?
q.explanation: The wind velocity (60 km/h east) is perpendicular to the plane's intended velocity (200 km/h north), so the resultant ground speed is found using Pythagoras: sqrt(200^2 + 60^2).

q.q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes a scalar quantity from a vector quantity?
options: A scalar has both magnitude and direction while a vector has magnitude only
A scalar has magnitude only while a vector has both magnitude and direction
A scalar can only be added using the parallelogram law while a vector cannot
Scalars and vectors both require direction to be fully described
q.explanation: By definition, a scalar quantity is fully described by magnitude alone, while a vector quantity requires both magnitude and a stated direction.

q.q: A vector quantity of magnitude 20 units is resolved into two perpendicular components. If one component makes an angle of 37° with the vector itself, which pair below correctly represents the two components (take sin 37° = 0.6, cos 37° = 0.8)?
q.explanation: The components are 20 cos 37° = 20 x 0.8 = 16 units and 20 sin 37° = 20 x 0.6 = 12 units, matching the first option.

q.q: A force F of 100 N is applied to a trolley at an angle of 53° to the horizontal ground, where cos 53° = 0.6 and sin 53° = 0.8. If this force is to be replaced by two equivalent forces acting one horizontally and one vertically, what are the magnitudes of these two forces respectively?
q.explanation: The horizontal component is F cos(53°) = 100 x 0.6 = 60 N, and the vertical component is F sin(53°) = 100 x 0.8 = 80 N, so the two equivalent forces are 60 N horizontal and 80 N vertical.
